intended_object: The complement X ∖ G of a set G of selected (generic) points in a topological space X, as a subspace with the induced topology. Inferred from the docstring and from how the module uses it in the generic-point-removal pushout square.
explanation:
The body `{x : X // x ∉ G}` is the subtype of points outside G. Its topology comes from Mathlib's `instTopologicalSpaceSubtype` instance, which is the induced (subspace) topology. So this is exactly the subspace X ∖ G, as the docstring says. It is definitionally the same as the coerced complement `↥(Gᶜ)` (`Set.Elem Gᶜ`), so there is no single named Mathlib declaration for it beyond that coercion.

The construction needs no hypotheses beyond a topological space and a set G. G is called "generic points" only because of how it is used later; the definition itself puts no condition on G, so it is fully general. Degenerate cases also behave correctly: G = ∅ gives all of X, and G = univ gives the empty space.

It is a thin local abbreviation, but it names a real mathematical object (the complement subspace) and does so correctly, so the verdict is faithful.
